title: Documented policies and procedures guide the care of patients in the Intensive care and high dependency units

13.1 Purpose: To ensure safe, ethical, evidence-based and holistic (Ayurvedic + modern supportive) care for all patients admitted to the ICU and HDU through standardized policies and procedures.

13.2 Scope:

This policy applies to

• Consultants: Ayurvedic and allopathic medicinal consultants

• Nurses

• Therapists

• Panchakarma staff

• Interns

• Intensive Care Unit (ICU)

• Emergency-linked critical care areas

13.3 Definitions

ICU: A specialized area with continuous monitoring, life-support equipment, and emergency response capability.

HDU: A step-down unit for patients requiring close monitoring but not full ICU support.

13.4. Admission Criteria

13.4.1 ICU Admission

Patients with any of the following:

• Hemodynamic instability

• Severe electrolyte imbalance

• Post-operative complications

• Severe sepsis

• Severe respiratory distress

• Neurological emergencies

• Any condition assessed and escalated by attending physician

• Severe life threatening conditions like renal failure, CCF, CV accidents, Burns will be referred to Apex Hospital, Nashik

13.4.2 HDU Admission

• Step-down from ICU

• Moderate hemodynamic instability

• Close monitoring after major surgical procedures

• Patients requiring frequent nursing care

• Uncontrolled symptoms needing close watch

13.5. Assessment & Monitoring

13.5.1 Initial Assessment

• Done by ICU/HDU physician within 30 minutes of admission

• Includes:

o Clinical examination

o Vitals, GCS, pain scale

o Risk scoring (APACHE/NEWS if applicable)

13.5.2 Ongoing Monitoring

• ICU: Continuous monitoring + hourly charting

• HDU: Vitals every 2–4 hours

• Strict documentation in:

o ICU flow chart

o Nursing notes

o Intervention sheet o Intake–Output chart

13.6. Treatment Plan:

Treatment is individualized and may include:

13.6.1 Modern Supportive Care

• Oxygen therapy

• IV fluids

• Emergency medications

• Resuscitation procedures

• Lab and radiologic support

13.6.2 Ayurvedic Supportive Care

• Appropriate internal medications if patient is conscious and well oriented

• External therapies like nasya, abhyang whenever necessary

• Ayurvedic diet and herbal decoctions

• Rasayana medication support for recovery

• Pain management through Ayurvedic modalities (e.g., lepa) where indicated

• Integration must prioritize patient safety.

13.7 Emergency Response Protocol

• ICU/HDU must maintain a 24×7 Rapid Response Team (RRT)

• Activation criteria include:

o Sudden drop in vitals o Loss of consciousness

o Respiratory distress

• Code Blue procedure to be followed for cardiac arrest

• Crash cart checks to be done daily and documented

13.8 Infection Control & Safety

• Hand hygiene compliance mandatory

• Aseptic techniques for all procedures

• Biomedical waste segregation

• Visitor restrictions

• Daily cleaning and fumigation protocol

• Surveillance of hospital-acquired infections (HAI)

13.9 Medication Management

• All medications to be checked for dose, expiry, allergies

• High-risk drugs labeled and double-checked

• Ayurvedic medicines stored separately with batch/expiry records

• Clear documentation of drug administration

13.10 Nutrition & Panchakarma

• Individualized diet plan

• Panchakarma therapy only after physician clearance

• Document each therapy in ICU/HDU procedure sheet

13.11 Patient & Family Communication

• Briefing during admission

• Daily update to family

• Informed consent for procedures

• Counselling regarding condition and prognosis

13.12 Discharge & Transfer Criteria

13.12.1 Transfer from ICU to HDU

• Hemodynamically stable

• Reduced oxygen/ventilation requirement

• Improved neurological status

• No emergency interventions in last 24 hrs

13.12.2 Discharge from HDU

• Stable vitals for 48 hrs

• Able to take oral medications/diet

• Cleared by treating consultant

• Transfer to ward with summary

13.13 Documentation Requirements

• Admission notes

• Daily progress notes

• Nursing charts

• Monitoring sheets

• Treatment orders

• Consent forms

• Handover registers

• Discharge/transfer summary

Documentation must be legible, real-time, dated & signed.

13.14 Staff Competency

• ICU/HDU staff must be trained in:

o Basic Life Support (BLS)

o Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS)

o Critical care nursing protocols

o Equipment usage

o Ayurvedic therapy safety in critical care Regular competency assessments and drills required.

13.15. Equipment & Maintenance

• Availability and functioning of:

o Monitors

o Oxygen supply

o Suction

o Defibrillator

o Nebulizer

o Infusion pumps

• Daily checklist to be maintained

• Biomedical engineering to handle breakdowns

13.16. Quality Indicators

• Mortality & morbidity rates

• HAI incidence

• Adverse drug events

• Code Blue response time

• Readmission to ICU within 48 hrs

• Documentation compliance

• Patient/family satisfaction
